President Donald J. Trump returns to Florida today to highlight a clear record of results that puts hardworking Americans first. Under President Trump and Republican leadership, Floridians are seeing historic tax relief, a surge in private investment and job creation, stronger rural healthcare, accelerated infrastructure and environmental progress, expanded support for veterans, and safer communities.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Floridians

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of Sunshine State workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 4.8 million Florida seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Florida taxpayers saw average refunds of $4,433 in 2026 — the highest of any state.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 399,000 Florida jobs, $73 billion in state GDP, and $36 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Expanding Workforce Opportunity: In September 2026, the Trump Administration approved Florida’s Workforce Pell Grant program, enabling students at Eastern Florida State College and other institutions to use Pell Grant funding for high-demand careers such as firefighting, corrections, and emergency management.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First policies are attracting significant private capital and creating high-quality jobs across Florida.

  • Johnson & Johnson is investing $1 billion to upgrade manufacturing and packaging technologies and build a new state-of-the-art distribution facility in Jacksonville.
  • Williams International is investing $1 billion to build a high-volume aviation gas turbine engine manufacturing facility in Okaloosa County.
  • Blue Origin is investing $600 million to expand its Rocket Park campus at Cape Canaveral Spaceport.
  • Lupin is investing $250 million to construct a new pharmaceutical manufacturing plant in Coral Springs.
  • Chick-fil-A is investing $150 million to build a new distribution center in Winter Haven.
  • Monin is investing $111 million to build a manufacturing plant in Zephyrhills.
  • Tampa Brass & Aluminum is investing $58 million in machinery and equipment at its Tampa headquarters.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Access

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand and modernize care in Florida’s rural communities.

  • Florida secured $210 million in first-year funding through the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program — the largest federal investment in rural healthcare in American history.
  • In August 2026, the state awarded $188 million in Rural Health Transformation Program grants across 31 rural counties. These funds support expanded access to care, growth of the rural healthcare workforce, preventive and home-based services, specialty and acute care, value-based care models, rural and satellite clinics, and health and lifestyle initiatives.

Investing in Florida’s Infrastructure and Natural Resources

President Trump is accelerating critical projects that protect Florida’s communities and natural resources while strengthening the state’s economy and readiness.

  • Accelerating Everglades Restoration: Working with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the Trump Administration modified key contracts to expedite the Everglades Agricultural Area Reservoir. The project is now on track for completion by 2029 — five years ahead of the previous timeline — improving water distribution to the Everglades, protecting drinking water supplies, and reducing harmful discharges.
  • Upgrading Critical Infrastructure: In October 2026, the Trump Administration awarded $85 million to upgrade 20 miles of I-4 highway between State Road 434 and State Road 472 in Seminole and Volusia counties. In August 2026, the Trump Administration awarded over $1 million to the Gulf Marine Corporation in Tampa for training center equipment, wheel loaders, and upgrades to three berths. In May 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration awarded President Donald J. Trump International Airport $10 million to expand the terminal and add new facilities for mothers and travelers with special needs.
  • Advancing Roadway Safety: Through Operation Highway Shield, the Trump Administration partnered with state and local law enforcement to conduct more than 3,300 inspections across Florida in just one month, focusing on unqualified foreign drivers operating commercial vehicles. 176 drivers were placed out of service, including 54 for language deficiencies, while dozens of others were arrested on criminal charges and immigration violations.
  • Delivering Disaster Relief: The Trump Administration has moved quickly to support Florida communities struck by disaster. In October 2026, President Trump authorized FEMA coordination following Hurricane Isaias. Earlier actions included more than $116 million to accelerate recovery after extreme storms, an increase in the federal cost-share for Hurricane Michael recovery, and nearly $416 million in additional disaster relief.
  • Funding Rail Safety: In September 2025, the Trump Administration released $42 million in four grants for critical rail safety projects along the Brightline corridor after the projects had been stalled in the Biden Administration’s backlog.
  • Advancing American Space Leadership: Artemis II launched from Florida’s Space Coast in April 2026. Artemis III is also scheduled to launch from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center, reinforcing Florida’s central role in America’s return to the Moon and beyond.

Honoring and Supporting Florida Veterans

President Trump is expanding resources that strengthen care, housing stability, and prevention services for the heroes who have served our nation.

  • In October 2026, the VA awarded more than $600,000 to Florida community organizations for adaptive sports programs that help veterans build independence, well-being, and quality of life.
  • In September 2026, the VA awarded more than $113 million in grants to 42 Florida organizations to assist veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless.
  • The VA also awarded more than $6 million to 12 Florida organizations providing suicide prevention services to veterans.
  • In June 2026, the VA broke ground on a new clinic in North Port that will replace the Port Charlotte clinic and serve more than 10,000 veterans annually.

Making Florida Safer and More Secure

President Trump is delivering decisive action that is driving down crime in Florida communities while securing the border and ending the failed policies of the past.

  • Historic Drops in Violent Crime: Violent crime declined across Florida last year, with murders down 19%. In Miami, in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, homicides plunged 50%, rapes dropped 22%, robberies fell 22%, and aggravated assaults declined 8%.
  • Securing the Border: The Trump Administration awarded Florida $608 million to expand illegal alien detention capacity. Catch-and-release has been fully ended, producing 17 straight months of zero releases at the border and zero Border Patrol releases in FY2026 — the first fiscal year in history with that result. Illegal southern border crossings were slashed by 95% from Biden-era levels in FY2026, the lowest total on record. Refugee admissions have also been sharply reduced.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, stronger rural healthcare, critical infrastructure, expanded veteran support, and safer communities. Floridians face a clear choice: continue this progress or return to higher taxes, open borders, and the failed policies of the past.

President Donald J. Trump returns to Iowa today to highlight a clear record of results for workers, families, seniors, farmers, and rural communities. Under President Trump and Republican leadership, Iowans are seeing historic tax relief, major private investment, stronger rural healthcare, and direct support for the producers who feed the country.

Delivering Historic Tax Relief for Iowans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering real relief to Hawkeye State workers, families, farmers, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 600,000 Iowa seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Iowa taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,365 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 57,000 Iowa jobs, $10 billion in state GDP, and $5 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Lowering Taxes for Family Farms: The Working Families Tax Cuts made the increased death tax exemption permanent and indexed it for inflation, helping keep generational farms in the family. The package also made 100% expensing permanent, doubled the Section 179 limit, made the 20% small business deduction permanent, expanded crop insurance, and increased reference prices for the first time in over a decade.
  • Expanding Workforce Grants: In August 2026, the Trump Administration approved the nation’s first Workforce Pell Grant program, allowing students at Iowa Central Community College to use Pell dollars for the Emergency Medical Technician program.

Standing with Iowa Farmers and Producers

President Trump’s America First agenda is delivering direct support, lower costs, and expanded markets to the farmers and producers who feed the country.

  • Year-Round E15 and Stronger Biofuels: In 2025, the Trump Administration cleared summer sales of E15 nationwide, waived all federal barriers to E10, and implemented the highest-ever renewable fuel volume requirements.
  • Historic Production: In 2025, Iowa farmers posted the state’s second-highest corn yield, a record corn production (2.77 billion bushels), a record soybean yield, and its third-highest soybean production.
  • Direct Relief: USDA has delivered more than $833 million to 57,000 Iowa farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program and more than $867 million in Farmer Bridge Assistance payments. The Trump Administration also announced an $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief program to help address temporary higher input costs and market disruptions.
  • Reducing Costs: President Trump suspended certain phosphate fertilizer duties, designated phosphate and potash as critical minerals, extended a Jones Act waiver to improve fertilizer logistics, and launched the $500 million FIELDS Program to expand domestic fertilizer production. The Administration also temporarily allowed off-road dyed diesel for highway use and deferred the federal excise tax to lower fuel costs.
  • Expanding Market Access: Ethanol exports reached a record high in 2025, up 13% from the year prior and 18% since President Trump returned to office, while U.S. food and agricultural exports have risen under expanded global market access.
  • Cutting Red Tape: President Trump’s “Right to Repair” effort allows farmers to lawfully repair their equipment, saving thousands of dollars per repair. The Administration also fixed diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) system issues that were forcing farm equipment and trucks to derate or shut down.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Across Iowa

President Trump is directing targeted resources to expand access and modernize care in Iowa’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: Iowa secured $209 million in first-year funding through the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program to expand clinical services, strengthen the rural health workforce, modernize technology and infrastructure, and improve coordination.
  • Modernizing Local Facilities: Funding from the program is supporting upgrades that include an MRI at Lucas County Health Center, a PET/CT system and new providers at Mahaska Health, a robotic bronchoscopy system at North Iowa Medical Center, expanded prenatal care at Sioux Center Health, a new CT scanner at Washington County Hospital, and a radiation oncology center at Wayne County Hospital.

Unleashing Private Investment and High-Quality Jobs

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and job creation across Iowa.

  • Mesabi Metallics announced a $15 billion investment to build a major steelmaking complex in Lee County, creating thousands of construction jobs and at least 1,750 permanent positions.
  • John Deere announced a $20 billion U.S. investment, including new high-horsepower tractor assembly lines at its Waterloo plant.
  • Google announced a $7 billion investment in cloud and Super Intelligence infrastructure in Iowa, including a new data center in Cedar Rapids and expansion in Council Bluffs.
  • Kraft Heinz announced a $3 billion investment in its U.S. manufacturing operations, including its Davenport distribution center.
  • JBS USA announced a $135 million investment in a production facility in Perry, expected to create hundreds of jobs.
  • Electrical Power Products announced a $42 million expansion of its engineered-to-order electrical power control and protection systems manufacturing facility in Des Moines, creating 200 jobs.
  • Greater Machining and Manufacturing announced a $16 million expansion in Independence, creating 100 jobs.
  • Webster City Custom Meats announced a $2.5 million expansion of its meat processing facility in Webster City.
  • S&J Tube announced a $2.4 million expansion in Wapello.
  • Protecting Ratepayers: Under President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, data center developers partnering with Alliant Energy, including QTS, must cover 100% of the energy and infrastructure costs for their facilities while supporting a five-year rate freeze for Iowans.
  • Restarting Duane Arnold: The Trump Administration announced a loan of up to $1.9 billion to NextEra to restart the Duane Arnold Energy Center, bringing Iowa’s only nuclear plant back online with 615 megawatts of baseload power — enough for nearly 500,000 homes.

Honoring and Supporting Iowa Veterans

President Trump is delivering targeted resources that strengthen care, housing stability, and prevention services for the veterans who have served our country.

  • In October 2026, the VA awarded funding to Iowa community organizations providing suicide prevention services to veterans.
  • In February 2026, the Iowa City VA Health Care System announced infrastructure upgrades, including a renovation of its dialysis unit, to support safe and effective patient care.
  • In September 2025, the VA awarded funding to five Iowa organizations to help veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless.

President Trump and Republican leadership are delivering lower taxes for working families and family farms, major private investment and high-quality jobs, stronger rural healthcare, critical support for farmers, and real resources for veterans. Iowans now face a choice: continue this record of results that puts workers, seniors, farmers, and communities first — or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies that put America last.

New Analysis Confirms President Trump’s Pro-Growth Policies Are Driving American Manufacturing Resurgence

President Donald J. Trump’s America First agenda is revitalizing American manufacturing, delivering historic investments, driving up wages, and igniting a blue-collar BOOM.

After the Biden Administration lost more than 200,000 American manufacturing jobs in its final two years due to reckless Democrat polices, President Trump is delivering on his promise to put American workers first. 

The results speak for themselves. New analysis by the Council of Economic Advisors (CEA) reports that wages are rising faster than inflation, domestic manufacturing is expanding, and the blue-collar jobs lost under the Biden Administration are rightly returning back to U.S. soil. 

Wages are outpacing inflation under President Trump, reversing the $3,000 annual decline in real wages under Biden. Since President Trump took office, blue-collar workers are seeing even bigger gains: manufacturing wages are up $2,000 and construction wages $2,800. 

Demand for factory construction workers is surging, hiring rising, and layoffs down over the past year. Overtime pay is also up— thanks to President Trump’s no-tax-on-overtime policy, workers are now keeping more of what they earn.

The benefits of President Trump’s pro-growth agenda and successful tariff policies extend beyond factory floors. This resurgence is strengthening America’s position in critical industries essential to our national security, including aerospace, aircraft equipment, metals, and natural gas and petroleum production. 

A stronger manufacturing sector means more opportunities for American workers, higher wages, and business expansion that supports Main Street economies who support communities across the country. 

BY THE NUMBERS

  • AMERICAN MANUFACTURING JOBS SURGING: Manufacturing employment is up 72,000 in 2026, including a 101,000 job increase in durable goods, reversing losses of more than 200,000 manufacturing jobs during the Biden Administration’s last two years. Since President Trump took office, construction employment has grown by 100,000, including more than 111,000 additional factory construction jobs.
  • RISE IN ANNUAL WAGES: Inflation-adjusted wages for blue-collar manufacturing workers have risen an average of $2,400 more per year since President Trump took office. Construction workers’ real wages are up  $3,800.
  • HIGHEST BUSINESS GROWTH IN 5 YEARS: U.S. business growth has reached its highest level in more than five years, while manufacturing expands and American goods exports are on track for a record year.
  • NO TAX ON OVERTIME: American construction workers are keeping more of what they earn thanks to No tax on overtime, with more than 29 million Americans claiming the deduction this filing season.
  • TRILLIONS IN INVESTMENTS SECURED: President Trump has secured trillions of dollars in investment commitments across the United States, supporting domestic production, factory expansion, and American jobs.
  • SMALL BUSINESS GROWTH: Small businesses and local economies are feeling the benefits of President Trump’s manufacturing boom.


    President Trump is driving a new era of economic opportunity, industrial strength, and national prosperity—unleashing America’s Golden Age.

President Donald J. Trump returns to South Carolina today to highlight a proven record of results that put workers, families, seniors, and communities first. Under President Trump and Republican leadership, South Carolinians are seeing historic tax relief, surging private investment and job creation, stronger rural healthcare, and major investments in infrastructure, military readiness, and public safety.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking South Carolinians

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of Palmetto State workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately one million South Carolina seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: South Carolina taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,476 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 86,000 South Carolina jobs, $15 billion in state GDP, and $8 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Opportunity Zones: In September 2026, Gov. Henry McMaster submitted South Carolina’s new Opportunity Zone nominations to the Treasury, made possible by the permanent extension of the program — unlocking new private capital and economic opportunity for communities statewide.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Access

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand access and modernize care in South Carolina’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: South Carolina secured $200 million in first-year funding through the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program.
  • Modernizing Care Delivery: In September, the state awarded $167.3 million in Rural Health Transformation Program grants to 228 rural providers for primary care, maternal care, pediatrics, and behavioral health — removing barriers and building long-term capacity through facility modernization, technology upgrades, and workforce development.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and high-quality job creation throughout the Palmetto State.

  • NorthMark Strategies is committing $2.8 billion to build a high-performance computing center in Spartanburg.
  • Octapharma is investing $1.5 billion to construct a critical care manufacturing facility in Rock Hill.
  • Ferrara Candy Company is investing $675 million to establish its first South Carolina operation in Orangeburg County.
  • Okonite is investing $400 million to build a new high-voltage electric cable plant in Orangeburg, creating 105 jobs.
  • Eaton is investing $340 million to expand U.S. transformer production in Jonesville.
  • Scout Motors is investing $300 million to develop a Supplier Park at its Blythewood Production Center and seven of its suppliers are investing more than $82 million across Spartanburg, Duncan, and Piedmont.
  • Adeptus USA is investing $215.6 million to launch its first South Carolina operation in Anderson County, creating 217 jobs.
  • TS Conductor is investing $134 million to open an advanced manufacturing facility in Hardeeville.
  • AmbioPharm is investing $119 million to expand peptide manufacturing and development at its Aiken County facility.
  • Rolls-Royce is investing $75 million to expand its Aiken manufacturing facility.
  • Red Metals is investing $70 million to establish a copper manufacturing operation in Charleston County.
  • Century Aluminum Co. is investing $50 million to restore its Berkeley County plant to full capacity for the first time in a decade.
  • George Utz Inc. is investing $40 million to build its first South Carolina manufacturing facility in Sumter County.
  • Re:Build is investing $20 million to open an advanced composites plant for aerospace and defense products in Rock Hill.
  • Tyson Steel is investing $15.2 million to establish its first South Carolina operation in Pickens County.
  • Coastal Precast Systems is investing $9 million to relocate its operations to Laurens County.
  • UFP Packaging is investing $5.3 million to open a wood packaging plant in Gaffney.

Investing in South Carolina Communities

President Trump is delivering targeted federal resources that strengthen roads, military installations, disaster recovery, and educational opportunity.

  • Strengthening Roads and Bridges: In July 2026, the Trump Administration awarded South Carolina a $23.5 million grant to replace 18 aging bridges across nine counties.
  • Modernizing Military Installations: The FY 2027 NDAA authorized $161.7 million for a nuclear power training facility expansion at Joint Base Charleston and extended funding totaling $166.7 million for new recruit barracks at Parris Island.
  • Delivering Disaster Recovery: In October 2026, President Trump approved South Carolina’s request to raise the federal share of Hurricane Helene Public Assistance recovery costs from 75% to 90%.
  • Supporting HBCUs: In September 2026, the Trump Administration awarded nearly $10 million to eight South Carolina HBCUs, led by $2.4 million to South Carolina State.

Making South Carolina Safe Again

President Trump and Republicans are delivering results that reduce crime and restore safety for South Carolina families.

  • Violent crime fell 11% and property crime fell 14% last year, including sharp drops in murders (17%), robberies (19%), aggravated assaults (9%), and burglaries (15%).
  • In Charleston, overall crime plunged 36% in 2025, with homicides down 29%, aggravated assaults down 16%, robberies down 24%, and sex offenses down 39% from the five-year average.
  • At least 72 law enforcement agencies, including the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division and the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, have signed 287(g) agreements with ICE to identify, detain, and remove violent illegal alien criminals from the state.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, stronger rural healthcare, critical infrastructure, and safer communities. South Carolinians face a clear choice: continue this progress, or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies of the past.

President Donald J. Trump returns to North Carolina today with a clear record of results that put Tar Heel families, workers, seniors, and communities first. Since taking office, the Trump Administration has driven down crime, returned money to workers’ and seniors’ pockets, and unleashed a surge of advanced manufacturing, pharmaceutical, aerospace, biotechnology, and SI investment across the state.

Making North Carolina Safe Again

The Trump Administration is restoring law and order — and the numbers prove it.

  • Nationwide, 2025 produced the largest annual drop in violent crime on record — a trend that continues to accelerate in 2026.
  • In North Carolina, crime fell across all four major categories in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, including a 12.4% drop in murders, an 18% drop in robberies, and a 23% drop in motor vehicle thefts. Statewide declines also occurred in 2025 versus 2024, including an 18% drop in homicides, a 21% drop in motor vehicle thefts, a 20% drop in robberies, and a 14% drop in aggravated assaults.
  • In Charlotte, overall crime fell 9% in 2025 and violent crime fell 21% (including a 13% drop in homicides, a 24% drop in robberies, and a 20% drop in aggravated assaults). In the first half of 2026, overall crime fell another 16%, violent crime fell 8%, and property crime fell 17%.
  • In Raleigh, violent crime and property crime dropped in the second quarter of this year versus last year, including a 33% drop in homicides.
  • In Wilmington, overall crime fell 16% in 2025, with violent crime down 17% and motor vehicle theft down 22%.
  • The Trump Administration is swiftly removing criminal illegal aliens from North Carolina communities. Operation Charlotte’s Web alone produced more than 1,300 arrests, including:
    • Armando Hernandez Martinez — an illegal from Mexico, convicted of homicide and cruelty toward a child — was arrested in Laurinburg.
    • Wilmer Marquez Benitez — an illegal from El Salvador, convicted of rape and a sex offense — was arrested in Raleigh.
    • Moises Guizar Alvarado — an illegal from Mexico, convicted of first-degree child rape, sex offenses, and taking indecent liberties with a child — was arrested in the Wilmington area.
    • Juan Dieguez Nolasco — an illegal from Guatemala, convicted of sexual assault, a weapons offense, damaging property, and dangerous drugs — was arrested in Raleigh.
    • Koffi Bassowou — an illegal from Togo, convicted of a sex offense against a child — was arrested in Charlotte.

Tax Relief for North Carolina Workers, Families, and Seniors

President Trump’s and Republicans’ historic Working Families Tax Cuts are putting money back where it belongs: in the pockets of the people who earned it.

  • No Tax on Social Security: About 1.9 million North Carolina seniors benefit from the new senior deduction.
  • Bigger Refunds: This filing season delivered larger refunds nationwide, with the average refund up more than 11%. In North Carolina, taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,542.
  • Rural Health Investments: North Carolina secured $213 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding — improving care for more than three million rural residents and supporting more than 400 rural health facilities. The state is positioned for nearly $1 billion over the next five years.
  • Protecting Jobs, Wages, and Growth: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 184,000 North Carolina jobs, $33 billion in state GDP, and $17 billion in workers’ wages.

An Investment Boom Across North Carolina

The Tar Heel State is winning in advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, aerospace, biotechnology, steel, and the infrastructure of the SI economy.

  • Amazon is investing $10 billion to expand cloud computing and SI infrastructure in Richmond County, creating at least 500 high-skilled jobs and supporting thousands more.
  • JetZero is investing $4.7 billion to build a commercial airplane factory in Greensboro, creating about 14,560 jobs — the largest job announcement in state history.
  • Johnson & Johnson is investing $2 billion to build a manufacturing campus in Wilson, creating more than 500 high-wage manufacturing jobs and thousands of construction jobs.
  • Genentech is investing $2 billion to expand its biomanufacturing facility in Holly Springs, supporting more than 500 manufacturing jobs and 1,500 construction jobs.
  • Biogen is investing $2 billion to expand manufacturing in North Carolina’s Research Triangle.
  • AbbVie is investing $1.4 billion to build a 185-acre pharmaceutical manufacturing campus in Durham, creating nearly 750 permanent jobs and more than 2,000 construction jobs.
  • Prysmian is investing $1 billion to expand its cable manufacturing facility in Catawba County, creating 385 jobs.
  • Vaxcyte is committing up to $1 billion to expand manufacturing and grow its workforce in the state.
  • Merck is investing $1 billion to build a new manufacturing facility in North Carolina.
  • US Forged Rings is investing $875 million to build a new production site in Hertford County, creating 625 jobs.
  • Novartis is investing $771 million to expand pharmaceutical manufacturing in North Carolina.
  • STERIS is investing $600 million to build a manufacturing and distribution hub in Sanford, creating 335 jobs.
  • Coinbase is opening a new office in Charlotte, creating 130 new jobs.

Results for All North Carolinians

President Trump is fighting for North Carolina workers, honoring the state’s military legacy, and delivering where previous Administrations failed.

  • Protecting North Carolina’s Furniture Industry: President Trump imposed Section 232 tariffs on imported wood products, including 25% on upholstered wooden furniture, 25% on kitchen cabinets and vanities, and 10% on softwood timber and lumber.
  • Honoring North Carolina’s Military Legacy: In 2025, the Trump Administration restored Fort Bragg — the U.S. Army’s largest post — to its original name, honoring Private Roland L. Bragg, who earned a Silver Star and Purple Heart for his courage at the Battle of the Bulge.
  • Delivering After Hurricane Helene: After the previous Administration botched the response, the Trump Administration provided more than $7.5 billion in federal disaster recovery funding to help North Carolina rebuild — and recently announced an additional $858 million to continue that effort.
  • Recognizing the Lumbee Tribe: President Trump delivered full federal recognition to the great Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina — fulfilling a promise he made on the campaign trail.

Thanks to President Trump and Republicans in Congress, North Carolina is stronger, safer, and more prosperous. North Carolinians now face a clear choice: build on the gains Republicans have delivered, or hand Radical Left Democrats the power to reverse them and bring the chaos back.

President Donald J. Trump was returned to office with a clear mandate to end the invasion that Democrats allowed to overwhelm communities, drain public resources, and endanger public safety. In less than two years, the Trump Administration has delivered the largest reduction in the illegal alien population in modern history, driven illegal crossings to an all-time low, and enacted sweeping reforms that finally put American citizens first.

Historic Progress: The Numbers

The Trump Administration reversed years of open border policies and produced the largest sustained drop in the illegal alien population in modern American history.

  • The illegal alien population has been reduced by at least 2.3 million, with more than three million migrants leaving the country during President Trump’s second term — the largest reduction in illegal immigration in modern history.
  • Nearly 1.2 million illegal aliens have been deported or removed, and nearly 1.3 million illegal alien arrests have been carried out.
  • The United States recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least 50 years.
  • Catch-and-release was ended, delivering 17 straight months of zero releases at the border and zero Border Patrol releases in FY2026 — the first fiscal year in U.S. history with that result.
  • Illegal southern border crossings were cut by 95% from Biden-era levels in FY2026, recording the lowest number of illegal border crossings in American history.
  • Nationwide encounters in FY2026 were the lowest in agency history (under 380,000), compared with roughly 2.7 million per year under Biden.
  • Entries by asylum seekers at U.S.-Mexico entry points have been slashed by 99.9%.
  • Asylum is now granted in just 7% of cases, down from more than 50% under Biden.
  • The immigration court backlog has been reduced from more than 4.18 million cases to under 3.09 million — the sharpest decrease in the Executive Office for Immigration Review’s history.
  • More than 12,100 gang members have been arrested, including more than 1,500 Tren de Aragua affiliates and nearly 2,000 MS-13 affiliates, along with more than 2,200 known or suspected terrorists (more than 2,000 of whom have been removed).
  • Nearly one million pounds of narcotics have been seized through Customs and Border Protection in FY2026 (63% above the prior four-year average), and more than 624,000 pounds have been interdicted by the U.S. Coast Guard, including more than 260,000 pounds of cocaine in Operation Pacific Viper alone — preventing over 219 million lethal doses from entering American communities.
  • Fentanyl trafficking at the southern border collapsed by 56%, and fentanyl-linked deaths plunged 22% in a single year.
  • Drug overdoses have fallen by more than 40% from the Biden-era peak.
  • America recorded its lowest overall death rate ever in 2025, driven in large part by sharp declines in drug fatalities.
  • Migration from majority-Muslim countries has been cut by 96% since 2024 and overall migration roughly in half, with visa issuances down 89% for Africa and 81% for the Middle East.
  • Border-related deaths fell nearly 80% in FY2026 compared to the Biden Administration
  • International student enrollment is projected to decrease by another 111,000 compared to last year.
  • More than 300,000 visas have been revoked, including at least 4,000 tied to birth tourism and 6,000 from foreign students who committed crimes or have ties to terrorism. More than 700 visas from Chinese nationals have been revoked by President Trump’s Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force since it launched in August.
  • More than 157,000 unaccompanied alien children who were lost under the Biden Administration — often to sex trafficking, forced labor, and other atrocities — have been located.

Securing the Southern Border

On Day One, the Trump Administration declared a national emergency, restored physical barriers, and deployed the military to restore control at the southern border.

  • President Trump declared a national border emergency on Day One and deployed thousands of military personnel to protect the southern border against invasion.
  • Border wall construction was immediately ordered to resume. Approximately 290 miles of new border barriers have been constructed, including 131 miles of primary wall, with $34.3 billion obligated from the Working Families Tax Cuts Act for Smart Wall projects.
  • The successful Remain in Mexico policy was reinstated.
  • The Trump Administration expanded third-country removal agreements with dozens of nations to expedite deportations, enabling the removal of more than 25,000 illegal aliens to countries other than their own.
  • The failed Biden-era CBP One app was repurposed into a self-deportation tool.
  • The Pentagon created National Defense Areas along the border in New Mexico and Texas, where illegal crossers can be charged with trespassing on a military installation.
  • Visa processing was paused for 75 high-risk countries, visa interview waiver categories were tightened to require most applicants to attend in-person interviews, and a new visa integrity fee along with several other new fees was implemented to enhance the integrity of the visa application process and deter overstays.
  • Temporary Protected Status was terminated for 13 countries, including Somalia, Venezuela, and Haiti.
  • Refugee resettlement was immediately suspended and the number of refugees admitted was dramatically reduced.
  • Illicit fentanyl and its core precursors were designated as Weapons of Mass Destruction, enabling harsher penalties, expanded seizure authorities, and treating this poison with the full force of national security tools.
  • The de minimis loophole was closed, ending the flow of millions of uninspected packages that traffickers used to smuggle fentanyl precursors and finished product into the country.
  • Migration through the Darién Gap collapsed by more than 99%, choking off a major transit route used under the prior administration.

Expanding Interior Enforcement and Accelerating Deportations

The Trump Administration has expanded enforcement capacity, accelerated removals, and targeted the criminal networks that exploit the border.

  • Immigration court hearings have been accelerated while welcoming the largest-ever class of new immigration judges.
  • The immigration enforcement workforce has been expanded, including more than doubling the number of ICE agents and record high Border Patrol staffing.
  • Federal immigration detention capacity has been dramatically expanded, including opening the largest migrant detention facility in U.S. history.
  • Deportation flights have been accelerated to record highs, and a record was set for the highest number of illegal aliens arrested in a month in August.
  • More than 2,500 agreements have been secured with state and local law enforcement under Immigration and Nationality Act Section 287(g).
  • President Trump signed the Laken Riley Act into law, requiring detention of illegal aliens charged with serious crimes.
  • President Trump invoked the Alien Enemies Act to expeditiously deport violent illegal alien gang members.
  • Over ten Latin American cartels were designated as terrorist groups, including Tren de Aragua, MS-13, and Clan del Golfo.
  • Major immigration enforcement operations were launched in cities around the country, including Metro Surge, Midway Blitz, and Catahoula Crunch.
  • The Victims of Immigration Crime Engagement Office was re-launched to assist Americans harmed by immigrant crime after it was shuttered under Biden.
  • The practice of conducting neighborhood investigations of potential new citizens was restored to verify their claims and ensure a full picture of their character.
  • Enforcement of the federal requirement that illegal aliens register with the government was resumed, with criminal penalties for those who refuse.
  • So-called sanctuary policies were terminated in Washington, D.C., while moving to strip federal funding from sanctuary jurisdictions.
  • A stipend program and fine program were launched to incentivize self-deportation and reduce costs.

Tightening Legal Migration and Protecting American Workers

The Trump Administration has reformed legal immigration pathways, ended abuses of temporary programs, and restored priority for American workers and wages.

  • Entry of H-1B aliens was restricted unless their petition is accompanied by a $100,000 payment, the random selection process for H-1B registrations was ended, and H-1B lottery registrations were driven down 38% for FY2027 under the new merit-based system, with no second selection planned.
  • Bonds of up to $15,000 were implemented for visa applications from citizens of high-risk countries, and student visa applicants are required to make their social media public for screening.
  • The practice of granting automatic extensions of employment authorization documents was ended.
  • Access to immigrant work permits was restricted, prioritizing U.S. workers and tightening security.
  • Employers’ ability to pay substandard wages to foreign workers in certain visa programs was ended to protect American workers.
  • A fixed time period of program completion or four years, whichever is shorter, was established for foreign students and exchange visitors.
  • The data schools must provide on students studying in the U.S. was significantly expanded, including information on programs of study, funding sources, graduation dates, and more.
  • The $1 million Trump Gold Card was launched as a path to residency for vetted, high-value applicants.
  • A new policy was established that generally requires aliens in the U.S. temporarily to return to their home countries to apply for a green card.
  • The citizenship test was reformed to better assess aliens’ understanding of American history, government, and values, and to better ensure aliens meet all eligibility requirements.
  • Naturalization fees were raised so American taxpayers are no longer subsidizing the process.
  • An unprecedented denaturalization effort was launched targeting those who fraudulently obtained U.S. citizenship.
  • President Trump signed an Executive Order ending birth tourism and launched a dedicated Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force that has already revoked thousands of visas.

Protecting Taxpayers, Communities, and the Rule of Law

The Trump Administration has closed access to taxpayer benefits for illegal aliens, strengthened verification systems, and secured legal authority to enforce immigration law.

  • Illegal aliens were banned from more than a dozen taxpayer-funded healthcare programs.
  • Foreign nationals — including green card holders — were banned from accessing Small Business Administration loans intended for American entrepreneurs.
  • Government-backed mortgage financing for illegal aliens and H-1B visa holders was ended.
  • The human trafficking hotline was upgraded.
  • Use of federal assistance and grant funding to provide services to illegal aliens was prohibited.
  • Illegal aliens were blocked from accessing federal funds for higher education programming.
  • Illegal aliens were barred from abusing refundable individual income tax credit benefits.
  • Data sharing programs on illegal aliens receiving taxpayer-funded health insurance benefits were commenced.
  • The financial system was secured against illegal aliens by urging financial institutions to detect and report illicit activity.
  • A new remittance tax was implemented on money sent out of the country by illegal aliens.
  • More than 206 million benefits eligibility checks were conducted in 2025.
  • The Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program was enhanced to ensure noncitizens cannot vote in U.S. elections while moving to purge tens of thousands of illegal aliens from states’ voter rolls.
  • Strict English proficiency and residency requirements were implemented for commercial driver’s license holders. The emergency removal of 110 commercial driver’s license schools associated with more than 5,000 drivers who failed English language proficiency tests was ordered, and more than 20,000 truckers who failed to meet enhanced English proficiency standards were removed from U.S. roads. As a result, traffic fatalities fell to record lows in 2025.
  • An aggressive crackdown on asylum fraud was launched.
  • A new visa restriction policy was implemented for family members and associates of individuals sanctioned over ties to fentanyl trafficking.
  • The Supreme Court affirmed the Trump Administration’s authority to remove green card holders who threaten American communities, upheld the policy to swiftly turn back illegal aliens seeking asylum before they set foot on U.S. soil, affirmed full discretion over Temporary Protected Status designations and terminations, allowed the Safe Third Country deportation program to continue, and allowed the Administration to end the Biden-era Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans (CHNV) parole scheme.
  • A federal appeals court affirmed the Trump Administration’s expedited removal policy, accelerating deportations of illegal aliens.
  • President Trump signed the Secure America Act into law, delivering $70 billion in vital homeland security funding for ICE and CBP.
  • President Trump signed the Working Families Tax Cuts into law, providing a record $165 billion for border security — including funding for border wall construction, expanded state and local law enforcement partnerships, reimbursements to states that suffered under the Biden-era crisis, and much more.
  • President Trump signed the Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026, into law, providing more than $18 billion for CBP, $10 billion for ICE, and $123 million for Citizenship and Immigration Services, and signed the Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025, providing a $485 million budget increase for ICE.
  • President Trump signed the HALT Fentanyl Act into law, permanently classifying fentanyl analogs as Schedule I drugs and closing chemical loopholes traffickers had exploited for years.

Today, President Donald J. Trump returns to Kansas to showcase his proven record of results that put Kansas workers, families, seniors, farmers, and communities first. Under the leadership of President Trump and Republicans, Kansans are benefiting from historic tax relief, surging private investment and job creation, stronger rural healthcare, major support for farmers and ranchers, and new investments in the state’s military installations.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Kansans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of Kansas workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 500,000 Kansas seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Kansas taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,453 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 53,000 Kansas jobs, $10 billion in state GDP, and $5 billion in workers’ wages.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand care in Kansas’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: Kansas secured $222 million in first-year funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program — the sixth-largest award among all states.
  • Modernizing Care Delivery: The Trump Administration awarded nearly $17 million to 14 rural Kansas providers to adopt new diagnostic tools and remote patient monitoring, plus $780,000 to improve patient transport between facilities.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and high-quality job creation throughout the Sunflower State.

  • Beale Infrastructure is investing $3 billion to build a data center campus in De Soto.
  • Merck Animal Health is investing $895 million to expand its De Soto manufacturing facility and R&D laboratories, creating 200 jobs.
  • Fiserv is investing $175 million to open a Strategic Fintech Hub in Overland Park, creating 2,000 jobs.
  • Indra Group is investing $50 million to build and equip a new manufacturing facility in Kansas City, creating 200 jobs.
  • U.S. Engineering Metalworks is investing $25 million to build a 110,000-square-foot production facility at Lawrence VenturePark, creating about 50 jobs.
  • J.M. Smucker Co. is investing $20.5 million to expand its Topeka pet food factory.
  • The Trump Administration awarded $34 million to the Kansas City BioSecure Manufacturing Tech Hub to build an advanced pharmaceutical manufacturing center and train workers in biomanufacturing.

Putting Kansas Farmers and Ranchers First

President Trump is delivering direct support, infrastructure upgrades, and market opportunities for Kansas agriculture.

  • Emergency Assistance: The Trump Administration has delivered more than $735 million to nearly 53,000 Kansas farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program for the 2024 crop year. Nearly 50,000 Kansas producers have also received more than $793 million in payments as part of a $12 billion national bridge program for trade disruptions and higher input costs left by the Biden Administration.
  • Support for Ranchers: In September 2026, President Trump signed two Executive Orders to back American ranchers — one directing action to help producers protect herds from wolves and other predators and advancing country-of-origin labeling transparency, and another strengthening enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act to expand market access without compromising food safety.
  • Infrastructure for Rural Communities: In September 2026, the Department of Transportation awarded more than $53 million to reconstruct and widen K-96 between I-135 and I-35 in Wichita, reducing travel times and improving access for school buses and emergency vehicles.
  • Year-Round E15: President Trump approved year-round E15 sales, expanding markets for Kansas corn growers and giving drivers more affordable options at the pump.

Investing in Kansas’s Military Installations

President Trump is delivering new resources to strengthen Kansas’s military bases and support the men and women who serve there.

  • At Fort Riley, the Trump Administration is investing $26 million for a new Air Traffic Control tower, $5.5 million to modernize security infrastructure surrounding the intermodal railyard, and $2.6 million to improve the staging area so the 1st Infantry Division can position equipment more efficiently for loading and unloading.
  • At Fort Leavenworth, the Trump Administration is investing $8 million to add a new fire station and $900,000 to update the current facility.
  • Forbes Field in Topeka was named one of four candidate bases in October 2026 for the KC-46A Pegasus mission, which would bring eight tanker aircraft to the Airmen of the 190th Air Refueling Wing.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, stronger support for farmers and rural communities, and new resources for Kansas’s military. Kansans face a clear choice: continue this progress, or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies of the past.

President Donald J. Trump and Vice President JD Vance are aggressively shutting down the waste, fraud, and abuse that has drained billions from American taxpayers. As head of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, Vice President Vance this week called on officials at every level of government to join him in a pledge to protect vulnerable Americans, keep taxpayer-funded benefits for Americans only, stop fraud before the money goes out, and hold fraudsters accountable.

From the Cabinet to the states to Congress, officials are lining up behind the pledge:

Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent: “I am taking @VP’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud. At Treasury, we follow the money. Over the past year, Treasury returned $175 million in payments that would have gone to deceased individuals and expanded Do Not Pay access to 99% of federal programs. Further, we stopped almost $190 million and returned over $100 million in funds that had gone overseas to U.S. victims. We ordered an audit of approximately $9 billion in Treasury contracts. And Treasury and the IRS proposed stronger eligibility checks for health insurance tax credits. In Minnesota, we took targeted measures to help ensure that taxpayer dollars reach the vulnerable Americans they are meant to support. And we continue working with U.S. banks to prevent government benefits fraud before it happens. But fraud does not stop at our borders, and neither do we. Overseas scam networks and cartels that prey on elderly Americans with fraud schemes are now sanctioned by the United States. Treasury is also making it easier for those with firsthand knowledge of fraud to expose it by accepting confidential whistleblower tips and offering cash rewards. If these fraudsters want to turn on each other, we welcome the assistance. The Trump Administration will not allow criminals, at home or abroad, to profit from programs intended to help vulnerable Americans.”

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth: “The War Department is waging war against waste, fraud, and abuse. Proud to stand alongside @POTUS, @VP, and @WHFraudTF.”

Attorney General Todd Blanche: “I’m proud to stand with @POTUS Trump and @VP Vance in the fight against fraud. At @TheJusticeDept, we are committed to investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people, no matter the size or scope of the scheme. We will not tolerate anyone who steals from hardworking, law-abiding Americans.”

Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum: “Proud to support @VP’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud. @Interior is cutting wasteful spending, terminating unnecessary contracts and streamlining bureaucracy to ensure taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly and deliver real value to the American people!”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “Protect taxpayers. Stop fraud. Preserve help for Americans who need it. 🇺🇸 I am signing @VP’s fraud pledge because every taxpayer dollar deserves accountability. At @USDA, we are committed to rooting out fraud across our programs and protecting assistance for the families who depend on it. Under @POTUS, we will keep fighting to ensure these programs serve the American people — and hold those who steal from them accountable.”

Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling: “Americans work too hard to have their hard-earned money stolen by fraudsters. Today, I am proud to sign @VP’s historic fraud pledge to send a clear message: Under @POTUS, @USDOL is FIGHTING BACK. With $22 BILLION in labor fraud already uncovered, we’re not slowing down. Alongside @USLaborIG and @WHFraudTF, we will leave no stone unturned in exposing fraud, recovering taxpayer dollars, and holding fraudsters accountable.”

Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.:“Today, I am proud to sign @VP Vance’s pledge and join President Trump and the @WHFraudTF in the fight against fraud, waste, and abuse. At HHS, we are protecting taxpayer dollars, holding fraudsters accountable, and making sure federal health and human services programs serve the Americans who depend on them. Every dollar stolen through fraud takes resources away from Americans in need. We will find it, stop it, and hold those responsible accountable.”

Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Scott Turner: “Under the Trump Administration, if you scam the American taxpayer and our most vulnerable, you will be CUT OFF and face JUSTICE. We are holding fraudsters accountable and putting law-abiding Americans FIRST.”

Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Dr. Mehmet Oz: “SIGNED! ✍️🇺🇸 @VP Vance’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud is a commonsense commitment, and I was glad to sign it. CMS will continue working with the @WHFraudTF to protect Americans, safeguard their benefits, and save taxpayers billions of dollars.”

Administrator of the Small Business Administration Kelly Loeffler: “I am proud to take @VP’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud. Under the leadership of President Trump, @SBAgov’s commitment is simple: we are restoring guardrails to protect taxpayer-funded programs, clawing back what was stolen, and putting fraudsters behind bars.”

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy: “ATTENTION FRAUDSTERS: USDOT is coming for you, and I am proud to join Vice President Vance’s pledge We’re CRACKING DOWN on… ❌ Illegal CDL mills, non-domiciled commercial driver’s licenses, and training schools ❌ Fake Chinese airbags ❌ Gavin Newsom’s Train to Nowhere …AND MUCH, MUCH MORE Signed, Sealed, and Delivered @VP @POTUS @WHFraudTF”

Secretary of Education Linda McMahon: “I am proud to sign @VP’s pledge and join @POTUS and @WHFraudTF in the fight against fraud, waste, and abuse. At @usedgov we have prevented more than $2 billion in student aid fraud and implemented real-time verification measures to protect taxpayer dollars. Every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar taken away from a student trying to build a better future.”

Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins: “Sign @DeptVetAffairs up! Proud to stand with @VP in the fight to protect Veterans and taxpayers from fraud.”

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin: “Taxpayer-funded programs must ONLY serve law-abiding Americans, NOT illegal aliens or fraudsters. I am proud to stand with @POTUS Trump, @VP Vance, and @WHFraudTF to fight fraud in ALL forms and protect the American people.”

Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency Lee Zeldin: “Amen @VP! Signed, sealed, and delivered. At the Trump EPA, since Day ONE, I have implemented a ZERO tolerance policy towards ANY waste and abuse, and the total savings from all our actions are over $30 BILLION!”

Director of the Office of Management and Budget Russ Vought: “Today, I am proud to sign the @VP’s pledge to protect Americans from fraud. OMB will continue to work hand in hand with the @WHFraudTF to root out waste, fraud, and abuse across the federal government.”

FBI Director Kash Patel: “This @FBI is proud to help lead the war on fraud under @POTUS, @VP, and the @WHFraudTF. We’ve worked with our law enforcement partners at every level eliminating tens of billions in intended fraud losses – including six Most Wanted Fraudster arrests worth over $2 billion in alleged fraud – all in just 3 months. American taxpayers deserve protection. Those who steal from them no longer have sanctuary.”

Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission Brendan Carr: “The FCC is pleased to join with President Trump and Vice President Vance in the fight against fraud. The FCC’s work on this front has already saved taxpayers many millions of dollars and we are working with @VP and @WHFraudTF to continue an unrelenting crackdown on fraudsters.”

Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor: “Today, I am proud to take the VP’s pledge and join President Trump and Vice President Vance in the fight against fraud. Together, we will ensure that American benefits programs serve only law-abiding Americans, not fraudsters and their enablers. Thank you @VP @WHFraudTF”

Administrator of the General Services Administration Ed Forst: “As part of the @WHFraudTF, I’m proud to take this pledge and stand with the @VP and @POTUS in the fight against fraud. Working together, the Trump Administration is weeding out waste, fraud, and abuse wherever it crops up – saving taxpayer dollars and ensuring transparency in each and every program. We will continue to put Americans first and place fraudsters on notice.”

Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency Cameron Hamilton: “Proud to join @SecMullinDHS, @VP & @WHFraudTF in pledging @FEMA’s commitment to protecting disaster survivors. Last year, we protected $1.3B in taxpayer funds from attempts to exploit FEMA programs. These efforts strengthen transparency and trust in federal disaster assistance.”

Vice Chair of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud Andrew Ferguson: “Proud to work with President Trump and Vice President Vance on this effort. 🫡 🦅 🇺🇸”

Executive Director of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud Scott Brady: “I am proud to sign @VP Vance’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud. We wage this War on Fraud to protect our most vulnerable fellow Americans and to preserve our benefits programs for future generations. Join us in this fight and sign the Pledge today! 🇺🇸”

Assistant Attorney General for Fraud Colin McDonald: “I am proud to sign @VP Vance’s pledge and join @POTUS and the @WHFraudTF in the fight against fraud. This is a fight we cannot lose. The wealth of America is being pillaged by sophisticated criminal actors who view our tax dollars as the easiest dollars to steal. There is no program too noble for a fraudster and no program too compassionate. Fraudsters will take from our elderly, our sick, our children, our hungry — no matter the financial cost or the human toll. At the National Fraud Enforcement Division (@DOJFraudDiv), we are resolved to do everything in our power to defeat fraud and protect the financial integrity of the United States. We are honored to sign @VP’s pledge and call on all public servants across the country to do the same.”

Under Secretary of Education Nicholas Kent: “Under @EDSecMcMahon’s leadership, @usedgov is the vanguard of the fight against fraud: 💰$2+ billion saved since January 2025. 🪪Instant verification for FAFSA. 💻Real-time data with partner agencies. Proud to sign @VP’s pledge to ensure American benefits stay out of the hands of fraudsters!”

Deputy Secretary of Homeland Security Troy Edgar: “Thank you @POTUS, @VP JD Vance and the @WHFraudTF for fighting fraud and protecting our taxpayer dollars. Americans work hard for their money, and they deserve a government that protects it.”

Deputy Secretary of Agriculture Stephen Vaden: “Proud to join @VP, @SecRollins, and the @WHFraudTF to pledge my support to fight benefits fraud. And remember, if you see something, say something.”

Deputy Administrator of the Small Business Administration Bill Briggs: “Today I’m proud to join @POTUS and @VP to ensure that American benefits programs only serve law-abiding Americans. The days of supporting fraudsters and their enablers is over. I’m signing the @VP’s pledge and will do all I can to fight fraud.”

Deputy Administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Kim Brandt: “ANOTHER SIGNED! ✍️🇺🇸 CMS’s own “Killer Kim” Brandt has signed the @VP’s Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud. Kim has been an incredible leader in CMS’s War on Fraud alongside the @WHFraudTF. Fraudsters: you do not want to end up in her crosshairs.”

Assistant Secretary of Health and Human Services for Family Support Alex Adams: “Today, I’m proud to take @VP’s pledge to fight fraud. At @ACFHHS, our responsibility is clear: protect taxpayer dollars and ensure benefits reach eligible children and families—not fraudsters. We are working with the @WHFraudTF across all our programs and tightening the bolts on our regulations that the Biden administration had loosened. I am grateful to the @VP for his leadership and commitment to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse across our government. We are just getting started.”

Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services T. March Bell: “Protecting beneficiaries and combating fraud are at the heart of HHS-OIG’s mission. I stand with @VP @SecKennedy @WHFraudTF in protecting Americans from fraud and reaffirm our dedication to safeguarding taxpayer dollars & holding fraudsters accountable.”

Inspector General of the Department of Labor Anthony D’Esposito: “Present for duty, @VP @JDVance. @USLaborIG has signed the pledge and remains in the fight alongside @Sonderling47 and @WHFraudTF. LFG. 🇺🇸”

Inspector General of the Department of Agriculture John Walk: “Today, I am proud to take the VP’s pledge and join President Trump and Vice President Vance in the fight against fraud. Today, President Donald J. Trump returns to the Peach State with a proven record of America First results that put Georgia workers, families, seniors, and communities first. Under the leadership of President Trump and Republicans, Georgians are seeing historic tax relief, a surge of private investment and job creation, lower energy costs, support for farmers, the most secure border in a generation, and safer streets.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Georgians

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of Georgia workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 1.8 million Georgia seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Georgia taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,169 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 198,000 Georgia jobs, $36 billion in state GDP, and $18 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Rural Health Investments: Georgia secured $219 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts.

Unleashing a Private Investment and Jobs Boom

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and high-quality job creation throughout the Peach State.

  • Pirelli is investing $1.2 billion to expand its Rome facility, creating 1,000 jobs.
  • Mayville Engineering Company is investing as much as $30 million to establish a new metal fabrication facility in Thomson.
  • Siemens is investing $185 million to build a new advanced manufacturing facility in Pendergrass, creating 1,400 jobs.
  • DeltaX is investing $141 million to establish its North American manufacturing headquarters in Walton County, creating 250 jobs.
  • ArcelorMittal Building Solutions is investing $107 million to build a new manufacturing facility in Macon-Bibb County.
  • Rideout Arsenal is investing $22 million to build a new manufacturing facility, creating 120 jobs.
  • Yancey Engineered Solutions is investing $5.7 million to build a new factory in Cordele, creating 300 jobs.
  • Unified Legacy is investing $125 million to construct a new manufacturing facility in Macon-Bibb County.
  • UCB is investing $2 billion to build a manufacturing facility in Gwinnett County.
  • Pratt & Whitney is investing $200 million to expand operations in Muscogee County.
  • Georgia is also positioned to capture a significant share of GE Appliances’ $3 billion U.S. investment, Thermo Fisher Scientific’s $2 billion U.S. investment, Silver Lake’s $400 million U.S. investment, Anheuser-Busch’s $300 million U.S. investment, and General Dynamics’ $200 million U.S. investment, among others.

Supporting Georgia Families, Farmers, and Communities

President Trump is shielding Georgia families from higher costs and delivering support where it is needed most.

  • Protecting Ratepayers: Georgia Power is freezing base rates through 2029 and delivering more than $2.8 billion in savings — $180 per year in savings for the typical residential consumer. Georgia’s major utilities have signed President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, ensuring large data centers — not Georgia ratepayers — pay for the power and infrastructure they require.
  • Delivering for Farmers: The Trump Administration has delivered more than $177 million to over 4,300 Georgia farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program and more than $171 million to over 4,000 producers under a $12 billion national bridge program for trade disruptions and higher input costs left by the Biden Administration.
  • Delivering Disaster Relief: After Hurricane Helene, President Trump raised the federal cost-share for Georgia disaster relief from 75% to 90%, approved a $318.3 million Disaster Declaration Request, and announced more than $1 billion in FEMA funding for communities and healthcare facilities.

Securing the Border and Ending the Biden-era Betrayal

President Trump ended the open borders policies that enabled tragedies like the murder of Laken Riley and restored the most secure border in a generation.

  • President Trump signed the Laken Riley Act into law, requiring detention of illegal immigrants charged with theft or violence — honoring the legacy of Laken Riley, a Georgia student murdered by an illegal alien previously released into the country.
  • The Trump Administration has not released a single illegal alien from the border into the U.S. interior for 17 straight months.
  • Refugee admissions are down nearly 90% from 2024 levels.
  • Southern border apprehensions in August were 94% lower than the monthly average under the Biden Administration.
  • The U.S. recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in half a century, with more than three million illegal aliens having left the country since President Trump returned to office.
  • ICE has arrested more than 10,000 gang members during President Trump’s second term.

Making Georgia’s Streets Safer

Crime is falling across Georgia as President Trump’s immigration enforcement, support for law enforcement, and tough-on-crime policies Make America Safe Again.

  • In Atlanta, murders dropped 22% last year and continued plunging in 2026 — with homicides down 36% in the first quarter compared to last year.
  • In DeKalb County, murders fell nearly 30% last year.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, support for ratepayers and farmers, a secure border, and safer communities. Georgians face a clear choice: continue this progress, or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies of the past.

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting money back in the pockets of Montana workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 200,000 Montana seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare

President Trump is bolstering access to care in Montana’s rural and frontier communities.

  • Rural Health Investments: Montana secured $233 million in first-year Rural Health Transformation Program funding from the Working Families Tax Cuts — the fourth-highest award among all states.
  • Rural EMS: The Trump Administration announced $8.7 million in September 2026 from the Rural Health Transformation Program for new ambulances and lifesaving equipment at 79 rural Montana EMS agencies, including three tribal governments.
  • Behavioral Health: Montana secured federal approval in May 2026 to stand up certified community behavioral health clinics at roughly 20 sites statewide, replacing short-term grants with permanent funding.

Growing Montana’s Manufacturing Base

President Trump’s pro-growth agenda is driving private investment and job creation across the state.

  • Janicki Industries selected Great Falls for an $800 million advanced manufacturing campus, creating more than 1,000 jobs within five years and more than 2,000 jobs at completion.
  • Montana ranked ninth in the nation for job growth during the first year of President Trump’s second term.
  • Under Republican leadership, Montana’s unemployment rate stood at 3.2% in August — well below the national average and ranking among the lowest in the country.

Driving American Energy Dominance

President Trump’s energy dominance agenda has reversed the previous Administration’s restrictions and unlocked major coal development that supports high-paying jobs and reliable power.

  • Spring Creek Mine (Big Horn County): In March 2025, the Department of the Interior approved an expansion that extends the mine’s operating life by 16 years, enables production of 39.9 million tons of coal, and supports hundreds of jobs.
  • Rosebud Mine (Rosebud and Treasure counties): Interior approved an expansion that recovers 33.75 million tons of federal coal, extends operations through 2039, supports more than 300 high-paying jobs, and supplies the Colstrip and Rosebud power plants, which together generate 1,500 megawatts of electricity.
  • Bull Mountains Mine: Interior approved a mining plan modification that authorizes 22.8 million tons of federal coal and 34.5 million tons of adjacent non-federal coal, extends the mine by up to nine years, supports more than 250 jobs, and enables significant exports to U.S. allies.

Building America’s Critical Minerals Supply Chain

President Trump is restoring domestic production of critical minerals and ending reliance on foreign adversaries.

  • United States Antimony Corporation (USAC) has earned millions in Department of War grant milestones for its Thompson Falls smelter expansion under a $27 million Defense Production Act award.

  • Montana antimony is refilling the National Defense Stockpile under a five-year, $245 million contract with the Defense Logistics Agency.

Returning Control of Lands and Water to Montanans

President Trump is putting decision-making back in the hands of Montanans while delivering critical infrastructure.

  • Grizzly Bears: The Fish and Wildlife Service proposed a rule in July 2026 giving Montana and other Western states greater flexibility to manage grizzlies in the Yellowstone ecosystem and other recovery areas where populations have met or exceeded recovery benchmarks, while maintaining Endangered Species Act protections.
  • Fort Peck Water: President Trump signed the Fort Peck rural water reauthorization in September 2026, keeping clean water construction on schedule for the Fort Peck Reservation and Roosevelt, Sheridan, Valley, and Daniels counties.
  • Crow Tribe Water Rights: Congress passed the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act in September 2026 and sent it to President Trump’s desk, giving the tribe flexibility to finish its water system and hydropower project.

Rebuilding America’s Nuclear Deterrent at Malmstrom AFB

President Trump is modernizing the land-based leg of the nuclear triad in Montana.

  • The Air Force and Army Corps of Engineers broke ground in May 2026 on a $26 million commercial entrance facility that clears the way for nearly $1 billion in Sentinel construction work at Malmstrom.
  • Work is advancing on surveying and preparing sites across central Montana’s missile fields to replace the aging Minuteman III with the new Sentinel ICBM.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering America First policies that put Montana first: lower taxes, major private investment, energy dominance, a secure critical minerals supply chain, safer communities, and critical infrastructure. Montanans face a clear choice between continuing this progress or returning to the higher taxes, energy restrictions, and failed policies of the past.

Today, President Donald J. Trump travels to Alaska. He returns to the Last Frontier with a proven record of results that put Alaskans first: lower taxes, responsible development of the state’s vast energy and mineral resources, safer communities, strong support for fisheries, and major investments that create jobs and reinforce America’s Arctic security.

Tax Relief That Puts Money Back in Alaskans’ Pockets

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering direct relief to Alaska workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Tips: Approximately 14,000 Alaska workers no longer pay federal income taxes on tips.
  • No Tax on Social Security: About 100,000 Alaska seniors benefit from the new senior deduction.

Unleashing Alaska’s Energy, Minerals, and Economic Potential

President Trump is reversing years of restrictions, unlocking responsible development of Alaska’s oil, gas, and critical minerals.

  • In October 2026, the Trump Administration secured $150 million in Defense Production Act funding for a major new power line that will lower energy costs for 75% of Alaskans.
  • In September 2026, President Trump unveiled a $200 billion South Korean investment in U.S. energy that includes $54 billion to construct a new natural gas pipeline in Alaska.
  • In December 2025, the Trump Administration reopened nearly 82% of the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska to oil and gas leasing.
  • In October 2025, the Trump Administration opened 1.56 million acres of the Coastal Plain to oil and gas leasing, reversing Biden-era restrictions.
  • In October 2025, President Trump approved the Ambler Road Project, providing essential access to the Ambler Mining District’s large deposits of copper, cobalt, gallium, germanium, and other critical minerals.
  • In June 2025, the Trump Administration advanced plans to open an additional seven million federally managed acres on the North Slope to new oil development.
  • In January 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order directing federal agencies to prioritize development of Alaska’s oil, gas, minerals, and other natural resources.

Protecting Alaska’s Communities, Fisheries, and Veterans

President Trump has moved quickly to restore historic names, support Alaska’s vital fishing industry, and expand care for the state’s veterans.

  • On his first day in office, President Trump restored the name Mount McKinley, reversing the Obama Administration’s 2015 change and returning the designation that stood from 1917.
  • The Trump Administration ensured Alaska groundfish fisheries opened on time, protecting a total value of $301.1 million for Gulf of Alaska fisheries and $2.64 billion for Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands fisheries.
  • The Trump Administration implemented regulatory and data collection reforms that allowed the timely opening of the Alaska halibut fishery.
  • The Department of Veterans Affairs awarded over $4 million in grants to community organizations supporting Alaska veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
  • In September 2026, the VA opened a new walk-in clinic at the Colonel Mary Louise Rasmuson Campus in Anchorage.

President Trump and Republicans in Congress have directed major new investments into Alaska’s bases, creating jobs and modernizing facilities that strengthen U.S. security in the Arctic.

  • President Trump signed the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, which included:
    • $208 million for new barracks at Fort Wainwright in Fairbanks.
    • $46 million for a base supply complex at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER) in Anchorage.
    • $152 million for the next phase of the Joint Integrated Test and Training Center at JBER.
    • $45 million to complete the Air Force runway extension at JBER.
    • $6.7 million to finish planning and design for a permanent party dormitory at Eielson Air Force Base.
    • $7.7 million to begin planning and design for a new Army dining facility at Fort Wainwright.
  • President Trump signed the FY 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, which delivered additional Alaska funding, including:
    • $82 million for the Air Force Joint Integrated Test & Training Center at JBER.
    • $80 million for upgraded Army barracks at Fort Wainwright.
    • $46 million for an Army Reserve Base Supply Complex at JBER.

    • $8 million for design of an Army dining facility at Fort Wainwright.
    • $1.75 million for design of an Air Force Coal Thaw Shed Addition at Eielson.
  • The FY 2027 NDAA, which has passed the House, includes $2.6 billion for Alaska and launches the multi-year, $7 billion “Fighter Town USA” recapitalization at JBER. The project will construct 26 modern facilities, position JBER as one of the most strategically important bases in the world, create up to 4,000 private-sector jobs, and bring additional military personnel and families to Alaska.
